author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Manchester officials and Harbor Care say the city has reached the benchmarks for effectively ending veteran homelessness after a two-year coordinated housing effort. The designation does not mean no veteran will ever become homeless in Manchester. Instead, the city says its response system can identify veterans quickly, connect them with services and move them into permanent housing so homelessness is rare, brief and nonrecurring.

The initiative began in September 2024, when officials counted 47 veterans experiencing homelessness. According to the city, every veteran in that original group later obtained permanent housing; one subsequently died. The wider effort has housed more than 130 veterans, with the city saying 136 people were placed through the coordinated initiative.

The Manchester Continuum of Care reviewed and certified the benchmarks. The system brings the city, Harbor Care, the Department of Veterans Affairs and community providers together around current case data and regular meetings. A Sustainability Fund helps address immediate barriers such as security deposits, application fees, temporary lodging and replacement identification.

Officials described the milestone as a measure of system performance rather than a declaration that the problem is permanently solved. Maintaining the designation will require continued coordination, available housing and resources for veterans who enter homelessness in the future.
dek: City officials and Harbor Care say a coordinated system has housed more than 130 veterans and can now make future homelessness rare, brief and nonrecurring.
headline: Manchester says it has effectively ended veteran homelessness
